correctness.rationale: For a finite spectral set, avoiding the countably many proper hyperplanes identifies the integer-character annihilators of the full and one-parameter phase-orbit closures. Torus character separation gives equality of phase closures and the exact 2δ Gram entry bound. The one-variable restriction is still normalized, real, globally nonnegative and positive definite. Adding a strictly positive constant and multiplying by a Gaussian yields an entire strictly positive Schwartz positive-definite function; its Fourier transform is an explicitly strictly positive finite Gaussian mixture. The error bound 2δ+2α+τD² tends to zero in the required order. All d,n>=1 and all boundaries are covered. The included verifier only illustrates these facts.

The latter are proved explicitly and not inferred from a title match.

value.rationale: The recent seven-variable strict obstruction exposes a natural gap: whether finite Gram inequalities and failures depend on the domain dimension or on atomic/periodic spectral regularity. The theorem resolves this for every finite positive-positive-definite trigonometric spectrum, every sample size, and every desired precision. It transfers strict obstructions into strictly positive one-dimensional Schwartz kernels with analytic everywhere-positive Fourier density, a substantially more regular function class than the motivating finite torus polynomial. It neither relies on a narrow arbitrary invariant nor assumes its separately reported numerical witness.
